newsitem.title: USA: Transitional Hospitals, Select to merge.
newsitem.headline: Transitional Hospitals, Select to merge.

text.p: Transitional Hospitals Corp said on Sunday it entered into a definitive merger pact with privately-held Select Medical Corp, under which Transitional shareholders would receive $14.55 per share in cash.
Based on Transitional's approximately 38.8 million shares outstanding, the deal was valued at about $564.54 million.

But Transitional Hospitals, formerly known as Community Psychiatric Centers, said after the merger agreement was signed with Select Medical that it had received a $15 per share cash offer from another major healthcare provider.

Transitional Hospitals said it had the right to terminate the merger agreement with Select on five days notice if its board determined the company had received a more favorable bid than the Select offer, and if Transitional and Select were unable to negotiate adjustments to their original agreement.
Transitional was not immediately available to comment further on the deal or to provide the name of the company which had indicated an interest in making the second offer.
Should it terminate the Select merger pact, Transitional Hospitals said it was required to pay Select a $19.4 million breakup fee.

Transitional said the other healthcare provider sent it a letter indicating it was prepared to buy Transitional in a transaction which would give Transitional shareholders $15 per share in cash. But Transitional said there was no assurance this provider would make a firm offer to buy the company at that or any other price.
The merger pact with Select was expected to be completed in about 90 days, the company said.
Completion was subject to certain terms and a two-thirds vote of approval from Transitional shareholders, it said.
Select Medical is a privately-held healthcare services company that was a recently formed in Mechanicsburg, Pa, Transitional said. Rocco Ortenzio is its chairman and chief executive officer.

The investment firms of Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe, Golder, Thoma, Cressey, Rauner and Ferrar Freeman Thompson & Co have committed financing to Select for the transaction, Transitional Hospitals said.

Transitional Hospitals delivers long-term acute care hospital services through a nationwide network of 16 hospitals and three satellite facilities with a total of 11,660 licensed beds in 13 states. The company also owns a 61 percent interest in Behavioral Healthcare Corp, a privately-held provider of psychiatric and behavioral health services in Nashville, Tenn.
